clue.text: Somewhere in existence is a name

parts.note: 'there' means present or existing somewhere, as in 'is there life on Mars?'
's is the short form of is

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing that some place in the real world holds a name.
explanation.walkthrough: THERE plus 'S (short for 'is') plus A spells out a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a common female given name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Hospital started during Depression is finished

indicators.note: the letter for hospital begins its life inside the other word, so it is put into it

parts.note: a trough is a depression, a low point between peaks
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital founded in the Depression years has now closed down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be through with something is to have finished it, so the word is a synonym of finished.

clue.text: Found bliss at the time going dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move around, so they are rearranged
with the time going, its letter is taken away from the word beside it

explanation.surface: Someone discovered happiness at that point by taking up dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' removes T from THE, leaving HE; 'dancing' rearranges BLISS + AT + HE into the answer. 'Found' looks like a past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, a direct synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Name the indefinite Spanish article

indicators.note: something indefinite is not fixed in form, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article, 'the'

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson asking for the name of the Spanish indefinite article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indefinite' rearranges THE into ETH; the surface pretends to ask about a grammar term (Spanish un/una), but EL is in fact the definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is an old-fashioned female given name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: He's set for a long spell as an upstanding native of South America

definitions.text: He's set for a long spell
definitions.meaning: The pseudonym of John Graham, who set Guardian crosswords for over fifty years

definitions.text: an upstanding native of South America
definitions.meaning: the monkey-puzzle tree genus, which grows tall and comes from Chile and Argentina

explanation.surface: A tribute to a long-serving fellow setter, presented as an upright South American.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian setter Araucaria took his pseudonym from the Latin name of the monkey-puzzle tree; 'upstanding' is the tree standing tall.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey-puzzle genus is a South American tree, and the pen name of a celebrated Guardian setter.

clue.text: Drake, possibly one getting on after very gutlessly grabbing duck

indicators.note: the person getting on comes after the rest in the answer
one part grabs the other, holding it inside
with its guts removed, only the first and last letters of the word remain

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, which looks like the letter O
an ager is someone growing older, getting on in years

explanation.surface: A male duck, perhaps, ageing and seizing a duck in a cowardly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutlessly' leaves only the first and last letters of 'very'. 'Drake' seems to be a male duck, but it is Sir Francis Drake, the Elizabethan sea voyager.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake sailed round the world, so he is an example of a seafaring traveller.

clue.text: Small bottle holding the last of Spirit of Life

indicators.note: the bottle holds a letter inside it

parts.note: a vial is a small glass bottle

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A tiny flask contains the final drops of a life-giving spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital comes from the Latin for life and means relating to life, as in vital signs.

clue.text: Audrey's excursion with Ron is not seasonal

indicators.note: an excursion is a wandering outing, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter: just the name

explanation.surface: Audrey and Ron go on a trip that isn't tied to the holiday season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excursion' signals that the letters of AUDREY and RON are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available all through the twelve months is not limited to one season.

clue.text: Clothes don't lie

definitions.meaning: an outfit, especially an unusual one
rise from bed rather than lying in it

explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is an outfit of clothes, and to get up is the opposite of lying in bed.

clue.text: Energy-producing device player of Egyptian god employed

parts.note: Re, also spelt Ra, is the Egyptian sun god
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A device for generating energy, worked by an actor playing an Egyptian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'employed' only join: an actor playing RE gives RE followed by ACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor generates energy from a controlled chain reaction, so it is an energy-producing device.

clue.text: Vessel's got a new number one — prepare to be sick!

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is replaced by a different one

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A boat has a new captain, and someone on board is about to throw up.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing the first letter of KETCH gives the answer; 'number one' looks like a captain or first mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave as if about to vomit, the body preparing to be sick.

clue.text: Perennial time to storm with anger, being incontinent

indicators.note: the letters for time and an angry outburst are placed within the continent

parts.note: read as 'in continent': ASIA is the continent that holds the rest
to rant is to rage loudly

explanation.surface: A garden plant takes its time to rage, while being unable to control itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incontinent' must be read as 'in continent', which is why 'being' is the container signal. Masterwort is the plant's common name.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrantia, or masterwort, is a hardy herbaceous plant that returns every year, an example of a perennial.

clue.text: Like a lifeline that ended up as a button

definitions.text: Like a lifeline that ended up as a button

parts.words: Like a lifeline that ended up as a button
parts.note: the cord linking a baby to its mother is a lifeline, and once cut its remnant becomes the belly button

explanation.definitionFit: The cord feeding a foetus is cut at birth, leaving the navel or belly button.

clue.text: Size up a house plant?

parts.note: 'size up' looks like 'assess', but means move a pot plant into a larger container

explanation.definitionFit: When a house plant outgrows its container it is moved to a larger pot, increasing the pot size.

clue.text: Port (Shanghai) fabricates houses

indicators.note: the words house the answer, holding it within their letters

explanation.surface: A seaport, the bracket explains, is where Shanghai builds houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts with Shanghai itself, but the answer is the Israeli port HAIFA, which sits across 'Shanghai fabricates'.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is Israel's main seaport on the Mediterranean, an example of a port.

clue.text: Lion tamer together with poor loser strangling head of circus

parts.note: 'and' joins things together

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap tightly round the inserted letter
a poor version of a word is a mangled one, so its letters are rearranged
points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A lion tamer teams up with a bad loser who throttles the ringmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' makes ROLES, which 'strangling' wraps round C. In the fable Androcles removed a thorn from a lion's paw and it later spared him.
explanation.definitionFit: Androcles befriended a lion by pulling a thorn from its paw, so he is a legendary lion tamer.

clue.text: Smuggler from isle (Lewis, say)

parts.note: Rum is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland
Carl Lewis was an Olympic sprinter, an example of a runner

explanation.surface: A smuggler comes from a Scottish island, Lewis for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lewis' looks like the Hebridean island, but it is Carl Lewis, the American Olympic sprinter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum-runner smuggled alcohol, especially during US Prohibition, so is a kind of smuggler.

clue.text: Mere mortals about to go wild for Norwegian spinner

indicators.note: letters going wild are thrown into a new order

parts.note: re is Latin for 'concerning', about

explanation.surface: Ordinary people are about to run riot over a Norwegian rotating thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MERE MORTALS are the answer's letters plus RE; with RE gone the rest rearrange. The original Maelstrom is a whirlpool off Norway's Lofoten Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moskstraumen whirlpool off Norway gave its name to all great whirlpools, which spin water round.

clue.text: Virgin takes delivery of foreign magazine

parts.note: virgin means fresh or unused, new
in cricket a yorker is a ball pitched right at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: The Virgin company is handed an overseas magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' only joins. A YORKER is a cricket delivery aimed at the batsman's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Yorker is an American weekly, so to a British setter it is a foreign magazine.

clue.text: The dreary stirring to make powdered food palatable?

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull mixing task to make dried food edible again.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried powdered food is made edible by adding water back, restoring the moisture it lost.

clue.text: Like a Dalek's pinch of the ear

parts.note: to pinch is slang for to steal, rob
otic means relating to the ear, as in otic drops

explanation.surface: A Dalek has a characteristic way of pinching an ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link (is). Daleks are the mechanical villains of the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Daleks are mechanised creatures that speak in a grating mechanical monotone, so they are machine-like.

clue.text: Ballet dancer kicking out left pin

indicators.note: kicking something out removes it from the word

parts.note: Sir Anthony Dowell is a British ballet dancer, former director of the Royal Ballet

explanation.surface: A ballerina high-kicks and leaves a pin behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden peg or pin used to join pieces in carpentry.

clue.text: Bush's networking set-up to beat Osama finally

parts.note: a LAN is a local area network of computers
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: President Bush's computer system set up to defeat Osama bin Laden at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' seems to be George W Bush, but it is a shrub; 's and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantana is a flowering tropical shrub, so it is an example of a bush.

clue.text: Money gets round Irish lad

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar, money
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Cash comes the way of a young Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucko is an Irish term for a young fellow or lad.

clue.text: What many people call their country cooking: yellowish, mushy, rather unappetising starters

definitions.text: What many people call their country

indicators.note: the starters of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A national dish is described as yellowish, mushy and rather unappetising.
explanation.walkthrough: CYMRU is the Welsh name for Wales, used by many Welsh speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymru is the Welsh-language name for Wales, the name its own people use for their country.

clue.text: Makes blue films' actors "non-operational"

parts.note: a film's actors are its cast; the possessive gives CAST'S
a computer that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Pornographic films' performers are out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like pornographic, but means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast down is to depress or dishearten someone, to make them feel blue.

clue.text: Raised to a higher power, like sugar used to be

definitions.meaning: raised to the third power in mathematics
sugar was once commonly sold in lumps shaped as cubes

explanation.definitionFit: A number multiplied by itself twice is cubed, and sugar once came as cube lumps.

clue.text: Fabric occupied a building

definitions.meaning: staged a sit-in, protesters occupying premises

explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy cloth, and sat in describes protesters occupying premises.

clue.text: Shirley secure in historic area of Dublin?

parts.note: Shirley Temple was a Hollywood child star
to bar a door is to secure it

explanation.surface: Shirley is safely ensconced in an old part of the Irish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only joins; Temple Bar is a cultural quarter in Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Temple Bar is an old riverside quarter of central Dublin, known for its cobbled streets.

clue.text: Term applied to eastern food outfit backed by Ford name

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a kit is an outfit, as in football kit
the Ka is a small car model made by Ford

explanation.surface: A word for an oriental dish, an outfit sponsored by Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Tikka describes Indian dishes of marinated meat cooked in pieces, as in chicken tikka.

clue.text: Tom, on date, sought sexual contact in public

parts.note: Tom Cruise is a Hollywood actor

explanation.surface: Tom Cruise on a date went looking for a public encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places D after CRUISE in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruising is slang for searching in public places for a casual sexual partner.

clue.text: Brummie's very into artist once worshipped by Rome

parts.note: Brummie is the setter, so 'Brummie's' is the setter's own, mine

indicators.note: one letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: The setter's very own artist was once revered in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is this puzzle's setter, so the possessive means 'mine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom, so she was once worshipped by the Romans.
